dailyUnits.objective: Design additive version tables, ownership relations, keys, and explicit delete behavior.
dailyUnits.whyNow: Historical planning data stays trustworthy only when versions and ownership are modeled explicitly.

steps.label: Model entities, immutable versions, keys, and ownership

dailyUnits.buildTask: Create an additive relational schema with ownership boundaries: model immutable versions, keys, relations, and delete behavior.
completionCriteria: Keys and foreign keys enforce the intended cardinality.
Update and delete behavior preserves retained historical versions.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the additive relational schema with ownership boundaries and tests for valid, conflicting, and delete cases.
rubric: Level 1: The relational schema permits mutable history, orphaned rows, or cross-owner relations.
Level 2: Additive versions, keys, and ownership boundaries enforce intended cardinality.
Level 3: SQL tests also prove retention under delete actions and reject ownership conflicts.

dailyUnits.objective: Create a strict runtime schema and infer request and result types without duplicating the contract.
dailyUnits.whyNow: Typed boundaries prevent untrusted payloads from silently becoming trusted application state.

steps.label: Define and exercise the strict request schema

dailyUnits.buildTask: Implement a strict schema plus inferred request/result types: model one UI action and every discriminated result.
completionCriteria: Unknown request fields and malformed values are rejected at runtime.
Every result variant is handled through exhaustive narrowing.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the strict schema plus inferred request and result types with typecheck and test evidence.
rubric: Level 1: The schema accepts unknown input or request and result types duplicate the runtime contract.
Level 2: The strict schema rejects malformed input and inferred types cover every result union.
Level 3: The contract also demonstrates exhaustive narrowing and a safe extension path.

dailyUnits.objective: Trace an accessible form submission from semantic controls through DOM events, HTTP exchange, and rendered response.
dailyUnits.whyNow: A reliable full-stack implementation starts with an accurate browser execution model.

steps.label: Build a labeled form and record the native event sequence

dailyUnits.buildTask: Build an accessible form with a documented request/event trace: annotate the flow from user action to rendered result.
completionCriteria: Every control has an accessible name and native submit behavior.
The trace distinguishes DOM events, network work, and rendering.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the accessible form artifact and a document containing the observed request and event trace.
rubric: Level 1: The form lacks an accessible name or the request-event trace skips a browser boundary.
Level 2: The accessible form and trace show the native event, request, response, and DOM update in order.
Level 3: The trace also explains cancellation, failure handling, and one browser-platform trade-off.

dailyUnits.objective: Build a form whose state transitions expose loading, success, validation, and retry behavior accessibly.
dailyUnits.whyNow: Explicit async states prevent stale UI, duplicate actions, and inaccessible feedback.

steps.label: Model state ownership and implement the async form

dailyUnits.buildTask: Build a tested form with loading, success, and recovery states: include accessible error feedback and duplicate-submit protection.
completionCriteria: Submission state has one owner and duplicate submits are blocked.
Tests observe loading, success, error, and successful retry.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the tested form with loading, success, error, and recovery states plus the focused React test report.
rubric: Level 1: The form hides loading state, permits duplicate submission, or cannot recover after an error.
Level 2: React state ownership yields observable loading, success, error, and successful retry behavior.
Level 3: Tests also prove accessible announcements and guard against stale async rendering.

dailyUnits.objective: Define and implement interaction states with semantic roles, keyboard behavior, focus visibility, and error relationships.
dailyUnits.whyNow: Reusable components amplify both accessibility strengths and defects across a product.

steps.label: Specify component states and keyboard transitions

dailyUnits.buildTask: Build a reusable component with visible focus and state text: add keyboard-safe input and programmatic error relationships.
completionCriteria: Keyboard behavior and focus order match the state contract.
Error and disabled states remain perceivable without color alone.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the reusable component with visible focus and state text, its state model, and keyboard test record.
rubric: Level 1: The component loses keyboard focus, hides a state in color, or disconnects error text.
Level 2: The reusable component follows its state model with visible focus and explicit state text.
Level 3: Tests also cover disabled, invalid, and recovery transitions without focus loss.

completionCriteria: Unknown request fields and malformed values are rejected at runtime.
Every result variant is handled through exhaustive narrowing.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the strict schema plus inferred request and result types with typecheck and test evidence.
rubric: Level 1: The schema accepts unknown input or request and result types duplicate the runtime contract.
Level 2: The strict schema rejects malformed input and inferred types cover every result union.
Level 3: The contract also demonstrates exhaustive narrowing and a safe extension path.

dailyUnits.objective: Create a strict runtime schema and infer request and result types without duplicating the contract.
dailyUnits.whyNow: Typed boundaries prevent untrusted payloads from silently becoming trusted application state.

dailyUnits.objective: Trace an accessible form submission from semantic controls through DOM events, HTTP exchange, and rendered response.
dailyUnits.whyNow: A reliable full-stack implementation starts with an accurate browser execution model.

steps.label: Build a labeled form and record the native event sequence

dailyUnits.buildTask: Build an accessible form with a documented request/event trace: annotate the flow from user action to rendered result.
completionCriteria: Every control has an accessible name and native submit behavior.
The trace distinguishes DOM events, network work, and rendering.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the accessible form artifact and a document containing the observed request and event trace.
rubric: Level 1: The form lacks an accessible name or the request-event trace skips a browser boundary.
Level 2: The accessible form and trace show the native event, request, response, and DOM update in order.
Level 3: The trace also explains cancellation, failure handling, and one browser-platform trade-off.

dailyUnits.objective: Build a form whose state transitions expose loading, success, validation, and retry behavior accessibly.
dailyUnits.whyNow: Explicit async states prevent stale UI, duplicate actions, and inaccessible feedback.

steps.label: Model state ownership and implement the async form

dailyUnits.buildTask: Build a tested form with loading, success, and recovery states: include accessible error feedback and duplicate-submit protection.
completionCriteria: Submission state has one owner and duplicate submits are blocked.
Tests observe loading, success, error, and successful retry.
dailyUnits.proofRequirement: Provide the tested form with loading, success, error, and recovery states plus the focused React test report.
rubric: Level 1: The form hides loading state, permits duplicate submission, or cannot recover after an error.
Level 2: React state ownership yields observable loading, success, error, and successful retry behavior.
Level 3: Tests also prove accessible announcements and guard against stale async rendering.
